title: New External DNS Resolver Usage
dataSources: UniFi controller events (`unifi:event`), Pi-hole query log (`pihole:query`), AdGuard Home (`adguard:query`), speedtest-cli results (`speedtest:result`), router/firewall syslog, ISP uptime probes (`uptime:probe`).
app: UniFi / router syslog, Pi-hole/AdGuard, and scheduled speedtests via HEC scripted inputs and the Universal Forwarder.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=pihole:query
| stats earliest(_time) as first_seen by upstream
| eval hours_since=round((now()-first_seen)/3600,1)
| where hours_since<24
| sort first_seen
description: Finds upstream resolvers that appeared only recently, useful for catching accidental config drift, VPN side effects, or a family device bypassing the usual path.
value: DNS changes are surprisingly good indicators of network drift; this inventory check keeps your resolver chain understandable.
implementation: Forward upstream metadata from Pi-hole; review newly seen resolvers and confirm whether they were intentional.
visualization: Inventory table of newly seen upstream resolvers.
grandmaExplanation: It ranks when a brand-new DNS server suddenly starts getting used by your home network.
